title: When Light Collides
caption: An Auxiliary Telescope under a multicoloured sky, Paranal Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A telescope in the foreground is lit by a yellow-green glow, while the sky above ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile runs through blues, purples, oranges, greens, yellows and reds. The telescope is one of the Auxiliary Telescopes of the Very Large Telescope (VLT).

The VLT has four of these auxiliaries, each 1.8 metres across, working alongside four much larger 8.2-metre Unit Telescopes. The Auxiliary Telescopes are self-contained and mobile. Depending on what an observing project needs, each one can be moved along a network of tracks to as many as 30 different observing positions.

When the telescopes work together as the VLT Interferometer, each gathers light from the same target and sends it through mirrors in underground tunnels to a shared focal point. Combining light in this way lets astronomers pick out much finer detail than a single telescope could manage.

understand.summary: A night landscape photograph of the observatory credited to ESO and Y. Beletsky. No camera or exposure details or colour mapping are published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures usually gather more light than the eye can, so the colours may not look the same to someone standing at the site.

explore: ESO calls the eight-telescope VLT the world's most advanced visible-light observatory. Its resolution is sharp enough to reveal detail on the surface of a star and to examine the region around a black hole. ESO titled the picture "When Light Collides".
alt: A Very Large Telescope Auxiliary Telescope bathed in a yellow-green glow beneath a sky of blues, purples, oranges, greens, yellows and reds.
